hints.title: Node Tilt Definition
hints.text: The tilt of a tree node is the absolute difference between the total sum of all left subtree node values and right subtree node values.

hints.title: Post-Order Subtree Summing
hints.text: Return subtree sums bottom-up while adding the absolute difference of left and right child sums to a global accumulator.

hints.title: Bottom-Up Tilt Aggregation
hints.text: Traverse post-order. Null nodes contribute sum 0. At each node, compute left_sum and right_sum. Add abs(left_sum - right_sum) to total tilt. Return node.val + left_sum + right_sum.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import Optional

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

class Solution:
    def findTilt(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
        total_tilt = 0

        def dfs(node: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
            nonlocal total_tilt
            if not node:
                return 0
            left_sum = dfs(node.left)
            right_sum = dfs(node.right)
            total_tilt += abs(left_sum - right_sum)
            return node.val + left_sum + right_sum

        dfs(root)
        return total_tilt
```

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Single bottom-up pass accumulating node tilts.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Re-summing entire subtrees top-down takes O(N^2) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Post-order recursion carries child sums directly in O(H) call stack.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Accumulate tilts globally while returning subtree sum in post-order.
